title: Australia (Oceania)
source: World Mapping 3.0 — Oceania, Australia (political), New Zealand, @sudarshangurjar

groups.name: Queensland
groups.mnemonic: Queen is Ban here — QUEENsland, BrisBANe

places.name: Micronesia
places.significance: The 'small islands' north of the equator — Palau, the Marshall Islands, Nauru, Kiribati and their neighbours

places.name: Melanesia
places.significance: The 'black islands' south of the equator — New Guinea, the Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, New Caledonia and Fiji

places.name: Polynesia
places.significance: The 'many islands' of the triangle from Hawaii to Easter Island and New Zealand — Samoa, Tonga, Tuvalu and more

places.name: Australia
places.significance: The world's smallest continent, with the island of Tasmania off its south-east

places.name: New Zealand
places.significance: The North and South Islands and the islands around them

places.name: Western Australia
places.significance: Australia's largest state, a third of the continent, and its mining heartland — Pilbara iron ore and Goldfields gold

places.name: South Australia
places.significance: The driest state, on the Great Australian Bight — Barossa Valley wine, and the uranium of Olympic Dam

places.name: Northern Territory
places.significance: A self-governing territory, not a state — the tropical Top End around Darwin and the Red Centre around Uluru

places.name: Queensland
places.significance: The Sunshine State — the Great Barrier Reef, sugarcane along the coast, and coal from the Bowen Basin

places.name: New South Wales
places.significance: Australia's most populous state and its first colony, founded at Sydney Cove in 1788

places.name: Victoria
places.significance: The smallest mainland state and the most densely peopled

places.name: Tasmania
places.significance: Australia's island state across the Bass Strait — mountainous, forested, and run largely on hydroelectric power

places.name: Canberra
places.significance: Capital of Australia — a planned city, built as the compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne

places.name: Perth
places.significance: Capital of Western Australia, among the most isolated big cities in the world, with its port at Fremantle

places.name: Adelaide
places.significance: Capital of South Australia, on Gulf St Vincent — gateway to the Barossa Valley wine country

places.name: Darwin
places.significance: Capital of the Northern Territory, on the Timor Sea — Australia's closest city to Asia

places.name: Brisbane
places.significance: Capital of Queensland and Australia's third-largest city

places.name: Sydney
places.significance: Capital of New South Wales and Australia's largest city — the Opera House and Harbour Bridge on Port Jackson

places.name: Melbourne
places.significance: Capital of Victoria and Australia's second city, on Port Phillip Bay — seat of the national government from 1901 to 1927

places.name: Hobart
places.significance: Capital of Tasmania, on the Derwent estuary — Australia's gateway to Antarctica

places.name: Cairns
places.significance: Tropical port and the main gateway to the Great Barrier Reef — the tourism hub of far north Queensland

places.name: Townsville
places.significance: North Queensland's largest city and port — ships out Mount Isa's copper, lead and zinc, and sugar; headquarters of the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority

places.name: Alice Springs
places.significance: The Red Centre's town, near the middle of the continent — gateway to Uluru, and the halfway stop of the Ghan railway between Adelaide and Darwin

places.name: Kalgoorlie
places.significance: Gold-rush town of the Goldfields, still mining — home of the Super Pit, one of Australia's biggest open-cut gold mines

places.name: Cape York Peninsula
places.significance: Australia's northernmost point, between the Gulf of Carpentaria and the Coral Sea — its tip looks across the Torres Strait to New Guinea

places.name: Great Barrier Reef
places.significance: The world's largest coral reef system, off Queensland in the Coral Sea

places.name: North Island
places.significance: New Zealand's volcanic island, home to three in four New Zealanders — and to Auckland and the capital, Wellington

places.name: South Island
places.significance: New Zealand's larger, mountainous island — glaciers, fiords and the sheep and wheat country of Canterbury

places.name: Stewart Island
places.significance: New Zealand's third island, across the Foveaux Strait — almost all of it the Rakiura National Park

places.name: Wellington
places.significance: Capital of New Zealand, on the Cook Strait — the southernmost capital of any sovereign state

places.name: Auckland
places.significance: New Zealand's largest city and an important port, on the North Island

places.name: Lyttelton
places.significance: Port of Christchurch, in a drowned volcanic crater on Banks Peninsula — the South Island's busiest port

places.name: Banks Peninsula
places.significance: Peninsula of two worn-down volcanoes on the South Island's east coast, sheltering Lyttelton's harbour

places.name: Port Moresby
places.significance: Capital and largest city of Papua New Guinea, on the Coral Sea coast
